title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN placed as the enemy hero: Salah ad-Din (1137-1193, Egypt/Syria) was born four decades after El Cid's death and never set foot in Iberia. The editor offered generic Kings, Saracen/Berber-flavoured units or an unnamed hero, so this was entirely avoidable.
Dialogue line 'Saladin's Emir' compounds the error by making the Ayyubid sultan the campaign's overlord in the taifa of Zaragoza.

Enemy roster of 28 CAMEL_RIDER and 31 CAVALRY_ARCHER is a Levantine/steppe army composition; Andalusi taifa and Almoravid forces fought as light lancers (jinetes), Berber infantry and javelineers, with camels essentially absent from Iberian battlefields.

King Alfonso VI of Castile, the man who exiled Rodrigo and the pivotal antagonist/patron of the period, is absent entirely; the Christian rivals El Cid actually fought for Zaragoza (Sancho Ramirez of Aragon, Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona at Almenar and Tevar) are replaced by a generic 'Traitor King'.
Two generic KING units stand in for named historical rulers (Al-Mutamin, Yusuf ibn Tashfin), so the ally who is repeatedly named in dialogue has no corresponding identified figure on the map.

issues_found: SALADIN is placed as the enemy leader ('Saladin's Emir', 'emir of the Almoravids'). Saladin was an Ayyubid Kurd ruling Egypt and Syria a century after El Cid's death (d. 1193); the Almoravid commanders El Cid faced were Berbers such as Yusuf ibn Tashfin or his nephew at Cuarte. AoE2 ships several Iberian-campaign heroes (King Alfonso, King Sancho, Imam, Count Julian) and generic units that could have been renamed, so this is avoidable.

Both active players are set to civilization RANDOM, so architecture and unit lines are not guaranteed to be Spanish/Saracen; the Iberian and Andalusi setting is not actually asserted in the scenario data.
King Alfonso VI, named in the narration as the man who exiled Rodrigo, appears nowhere as an object despite a KING_ALFONSO hero existing in the engine.

Enemy army is 28 camel riders plus 31 cavalry archers with no infantry; Almoravid armies were built on Berber and Andalusi light cavalry, spear infantry and drum-and-javelin foot, and camel riders in Iberia are essentially unattested.

Player 1's 'small retinue' (El Cid plus 16 troops, a Town Center, Barracks, Stable, Archery Range and Blacksmith) is a standard build-order base rather than a landless exile's warband; the brief's growth-through-victory is handled only by CHANGE_OWNERSHIP triggers.

The narrative spine is generic scripted-campaign filler: 'Ambusher', 'Traitor King', 'Rescued Ally', 'Final Ally', an invented betrayal and a fortress breach. The actual turning points — the victory over Aragon and Berenguer Ramon II at Almenar/Tevar, the capture of the Cid's Castilian rival, the 1094 siege and taking of Valencia, and the defence at Cuarte in 1094 — are absent.
Valencia, the stated culmination of the brief, is never named in the in-game text or encoded in any condition; the final target is an anonymous 'enemy stronghold'.

Defeat is also triggered by the death of Player 3's KING (Al-Mutamin). Al-Mutamin died naturally in 1085 and his death did not end El Cid's career; the Cid simply continued serving his son al-Musta'in.
Victory on destroying a single GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH inside an area is an engine bookkeeping condition, not the historical goal of taking and holding a city.

SALADIN is placed as the enemy hero and the primary victory target; Saladin (d. 1193, Ayyubid Egypt/Syria) never fought in Iberia and belongs to a different culture and a century later than the Almoravid emirs (Yusuf ibn Tashfin) or the taifa rivals El Cid actually faced. The engine offers other Muslim/Iberian-appropriate heroes or a simple renamed generic unit, so this was avoidable.
Both active players are set to civilization RANDOM, so architecture and unit sets are not fixed as Spanish and Saracen/Berber; the Iberian setting is left to chance.
Al-Mutamin of Zaragoza, El Cid's actual patron, exists only as a dialogue line and an anonymous KING; Alfonso VI and Yusuf ibn Tashfin are absent entirely.

Player 2's army is 28 camel riders and 31 cavalry archers with no infantry — a steppe/Saracen composition rather than Almoravid Berber infantry-and-lancer forces, and vastly outnumbering any force El Cid faced at this stage.

Central plot beats are invented: a 'Traitor King' betrayal, a generic raider outpost, and a rescued ally, none of which correspond to the Zaragoza campaigns (Almenar, Morella) or the 1094 siege of Valencia.
Valencia — the stated culmination of the brief — is nowhere in the victory conditions; the campaign instead ends at a generic 'enemy fortress' with an Almoravid/Saladin emir.
Alternative victory fires on destroying a GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH inside an arbitrary map area, an objective the history does not single out.
Defeat is tied to the death of a nameless Player 3 KING labelled 'key ally'; El Cid's fortunes never hinged on protecting a Muslim king's life in this way.
